subject: Emotions
title: Micro-Joys
description: A short lesson to help you apply Micro-Joys.

hook.text: Japanese researcher Sonja Lyubomirsky found that frequent small pleasures predict happiness better than rare big ones.

buildup.text: Micro-joys are tiny positive moments: morning coffee, a good song, sunshine on skin. Most days contain dozens.

discovery.text: The brain processes many small positives more effectively than one large one. Frequency beats intensity for well-being.

twist.text: Most people ignore micro-joys because they seem unremarkable. Training attention to notice them shifts the baseline.

climax.text: The happiest people aren't having extraordinary lives. They're noticing ordinary pleasures others walk past.

punchline.text: Joy hides in the ordinary. Attention finds it.

quiz.question: What predicts happiness better: rare big events or frequent small ones?
